description: 6-turn backup-planning conversation alternating xhigh/low reasoning effort. Coherence is testable: turns 3-6 only make sense if the model carries forward decisions from earlier turns (restic/WireGuard choice, CGNAT inversion, 5 Mbps math).

turns.question: ok so here is the thing, I have a home server, well actually two if you count the old laptop, and I want to back up my photos, but ALSO I do not want to pay for cloud storage because reasons, and my sister has a NAS at her place across town, and I was thinking maybe syncthing? or maybe rsync over a VPN? or wireguard something something... but then what happens when her NAS dies, do I need a third copy? people say 3-2-1 backup but honestly who has the time, and should the backups be encrypted before they leave my machine because I do not want my sister seeing my memes folder... anyway WHAT should I actually set up, give me a concrete recommendation, not seventeen options.
and what if my sister moves abroad, does anything change?
ok she moved and took the NAS, but her new ISP is doing CGNAT so no port forwarding on her side at all. rework the plan around that, and remember I still refuse to pay for cloud anything.
so which of the two ends initiates the tunnel then, mine or hers?

new wrinkle: my upload is 5 Mbps and the photo library is 800GB and growing about 20GB a year. give me a realistic migration plan with actual numbers, how long the initial seed takes, whether I should seed the first copy onto a disk and mail it to her, all of it.
summarize the final setup in five bullet points.
